newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Hun Sen says prince no longer premier.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen says prince no longer premier.

text.p: Cambodia's strongman Hun Sen said on Sunday his rival, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, was no longer prime minister, unilaterally ousting the prince from their shattered coalition government.

Hun Sen, speaking in a radio broadcast after a day of heavy fighting on the streets of Phnom Penh between his troops and those loyal to Ranariddh, called on breakaway dissidents from Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party to fill the prince's post of First Prime Minister.
"The government is ready to choose a new First Prime Minister," Hun Sen said.
"The position of first prime minister is in FUNCINPEC's quota so let FUNCINPEC adopt a political figure," he said. Hun Sen said he did not want the post of first prime minister.
Fighting erupted between Hun Sen's forces and those loyal to First Prime Minister Ranariddh on Saturday and continued through Sunday, leaving at least 12 people dead and more than 50 wounded.
The prince, whose FUNCINPEC party won a 1993 election organised by the United Nations, said in a statement from Paris on Saturday that Hun Sen had launched a coup against him.
